verdict.falsifier: Brendan's reading: src/rsr/train/loop.py's policy_name='rsr' and policy_name='fifo' runs are the SAME arm -- train() stamps policy_name into run_id and the frozen config but constructs FIFOPolicy() unconditionally (loop.py:138), so a heartbeat reading "policy": "rsr" is a FIFO run. The reading dies if two runs at identical seed and config, differing only in policy_name, have trajectories that differ by more than the run-to-run floor.
verdict.detail: Could not be falsified. On CPU (deterministic) the fifo and rsr loss sequences are BIT-IDENTICAL over all 10 beats (max|dloss| = 0.0) while config_hash and run_id differ. On MPS they differ by 3.1789143850602386e-07, but the fifo-vs-fifo REPLICATE at the same seed differs by exactly the same 3.1789143850602386e-07, so that is the nondeterminism floor, not policy signal. The heartbeat header of the rsr runs reads "policy": "rsr" and their beats carry attribution=null, because FIFOPolicy has no attribution() method. This is corpus-sheet defect 2's shape relocated from RSRConfig into the training loop. Separately measured: bypassing five walls, the RSR eviction path DOES run -- 256 evictions, attribution {'psi': 256} with zero fifo_warmup, disagreeing with FIFO on 239/256 identical memory states and moving a forward-only loss by 0.0806427001953125 -- so a real RSR arm would produce a visibly different trajectory, and the loop is not producing one.
